newsitem.title: USA: Senate group votes 52 subpoenas in campaign probe.
newsitem.headline: Senate group votes 52 subpoenas in campaign probe.

text.p: The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee investigating campaign finance abuses voted Thursday to issue its first 52 subpoenas for documents focusing on foreign fundraising in the 1996 election.

The Republican-controlled committee approved 43 of the subpoenas without objections from Democrats on a 16 to 0 vote. Democrats balked at nine other subpoenas, but the committee approved them nevertheless on a partisan 9 to 7 vote.

Democrats led by Sen. John Glenn, of Ohio, said the subpoenas seemed almost entirely aimed at their party when there had been promises of a bipartisan investigation. Committee chairman Fred Thompson, a Tennessee Republican, said objections from Democrats were just more "resistance" from that party.
"The subpoenas seemed to focus almost exclusively on the Clinton campaign operation," New Jersey Democratic Sen. Robert Torricelli said after the hour-long committee session.
Many of the names of people and companies on the subpoena list made available appeared Asian and included affiliated firms of the Lippo Group, a large Indonesian investment firm.

The committee plans to look into news reports of of illegal or improper fundraising from Asian groups or people with foreign business interests. The subpoena list also included telephone records and demands for material from the State and Commerce Departments, the White House Office of Personnel Management and the Comptroller of the Currency.
